issues.legal_issue: Punishment for contempt requires wilful or deliberate disobedience of a court order, and the respondent’s failure to hand over possession in the circumstances did not meet that standard.
material_facts: An earlier order required the respondent to hand over possession within a specified period, unless it obtained a court order or acquired an independent right to retain possession.
Within that period, the government began formal proceedings to acquire the premises and authorised steps to take possession.
While the acquisition was challenged, another court ordered that possession remain unchanged, preventing the acquisition from proceeding unless that order was vacated.
The respondent remained in possession, and the petitioner sought punishment for contempt.
issues.conclusion: The respondent had not wilfully, deliberately, or recklessly disobeyed the earlier order, so the contempt petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, contempt for disobedience requires wilful or deliberate disobedience of a court order. The Court applied that requirement and found no such disobedience in the circumstances. No earlier case was cited as authority for this contempt rule; H.D. Vora v. State of Maharashtra was discussed as background on the distinction between temporary requisition and acquisition.

rule.if: contempt_proceeding and conditional_handover_order and acquisition_steps_taken and status_quo_restraint and not wilful_disobedience

predicates.contempt_proceeding: A party brought a proceeding seeking punishment for alleged disobedience of a court order.
predicates.conditional_handover_order: The court ordered handover within a specified period unless the respondent obtained a court order or acquired an independent right to retain possession.
predicates.acquisition_steps_taken: The government began formal acquisition steps concerning the property during the handover period.
predicates.status_quo_restraint: A court ordered that possession remain unchanged while the acquisition was challenged.
predicates.wilful_disobedience: The respondent deliberately, wilfully, or recklessly failed to obey the court order.
predicates.contempt_not_established: The alleged disobedience does not amount to contempt.

issues.definition: When a contempt proceeding concerns a conditional handover order, acquisition steps were taken, possession was subject to a court-ordered restraint, and the failure to hand over was not wilful, contempt is not established.

issues.legal_issue: An additional deposit for continued use of property may be ordered while a challenge to the basis for retaining possession remains pending, to address the possibility that the occupant will remain after it should have surrendered possession.
material_facts: The respondent continued to occupy the premises while the validity of the acquisition remained under challenge in a pending writ proceeding.
The Court recognised that, if the petitioner succeeded in that proceeding, the respondent would have remained in possession beyond the time when possession should have been handed over.
The respondent was already paying monthly compensation for use of the premises under an earlier order.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed the respondent to deposit an additional monthly amount in court, in addition to the compensation already being paid, with the deposits to be invested by the Registrar-General.
issues.legal_principle: The Court made an interim direction to address the risk of continued occupation if the pending challenge succeeded. It cited no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this direction.

rule.if: pending_writ_case and continued_occupancy and petitioner_may_succeed and existing_use_compensation_order

predicates.pending_writ_case: A writ proceeding challenging the basis for retaining possession remains pending.
predicates.continued_occupancy: The respondent continues to occupy the property while that proceeding is pending.
predicates.petitioner_may_succeed: The petitioner may succeed in the pending proceeding, in which case the respondent will have occupied the property after possession should have been surrendered.
predicates.existing_use_compensation_order: A court has already ordered the occupant to pay compensation for continued use of the property.
predicates.additional_use_compensation_deposit_orde: The occupant is directed to make an additional deposit for continued use of the property.

issues.definition: When a writ challenge remains pending, the respondent continues to occupy the property, the petitioner may succeed, and compensation is already ordered, an additional deposit for use of the property may be required.
